title: Toolara Summarize
heroTitle: Long articles, key points in seconds
heroPreviewBody:
Summary (medium)

• Remote work cut commute time by 42% on average
• Teams report fewer interruptions, slower decisions
• Hybrid schedules won on retention in 6 of 8 studies
subtitle: Paste any article, email, or document. Get a concise summary in seconds.
resultDisclaimer: AI summaries can miss nuance. Review the full source for important decisions.
whatIsText: Long documents take time to read. This tool uses a large language model to extract the core message and condense it into a summary — short, medium, or long, depending on your needs. It works on articles, emails, reports, transcripts, and any other text you need to digest quickly.
use1: Articles and blog posts — Get the gist before deciding to read the full piece.
use2: Long emails — Extract the key asks and action items from verbose threads.
use3: Research papers — Understand the abstract and main findings without reading everything.
use4: Meeting transcripts — Turn an hour of conversation into a usable recap.
use5: Reports and documentation — Quickly grasp structure and conclusions.
faq1a: Yes. The tool runs on Cloudflare Workers AI with a free daily quota. Normal personal use won't hit any limits.
faq2a: No. Your text is processed in memory and discarded. Nothing is stored, logged, or used for training.
faq3q: What is the maximum input length?
faq3a: 8,000 characters per request. Longer inputs are truncated to the first 8,000 characters. For very long documents, split them into sections and summarize each.
faq4a: The model captures the main points reliably. However, summaries can miss nuance, omit important caveats, or misread ambiguous phrasing. For critical decisions, always read the original.
faq5a: We use Meta's Llama 3.2 3B model, running on Cloudflare's global edge network. It's fast and capable for summarization tasks.
disclaimer: Disclaimer: Do not use summaries as a substitute for reading legal, medical, or financial documents in full.
footer: Runs on Cloudflare Workers AI. Your text is not stored.
errGeneric: Something went wrong. Please try again.
errRateLimit: Too many requests. Please wait a minute and try again.
f1d: Articles, reports, emails and transcripts — up to 8,000 characters per run.
f2d: From a one-line TL;DR to a structured recap — pick the depth you need.
f3d: The model extracts the core message instead of trimming sentences at random.
ph1: Paste your article, email, or document here...
howIntro: Paste the source, pick a length, copy the bullets. No account needed.
how1d: Articles, PDFs copied as text, meeting notes, or a long email thread. Up to roughly 8,000 words in one pass.
how2d: Short gives you one or two sentences. Medium gives a handful of bullets. Detailed keeps sub-points and numbers.
how3d: Every summary is bullet-based so you can paste it into Slack, a doc, or your own notes without reformatting.
use1d: Skim three summaries before deciding which article deserves a full read.
use2t: Meeting notes need to become decisions
use2d: Summarise the raw notes, then keep the bullets that name an owner or a deadline.
use3d: Drop in a competitor page or a long report and get the claims you need to respond to.
use4d: Paste the thread, read four bullets, and reply to the actual question.

faq6q: How long can the input be?
faq6a: Around 8,000 words per request. Longer documents are better handled in sections, since the model keeps more detail when the input is focused.
faq7q: Does it keep numbers and quotes?
faq7a: Yes, when you choose Medium or Detailed. Short mode favours compression and may drop supporting figures.
faq8a: Copy the text out of the PDF and paste it in. Scanned pages without selectable text need OCR first.
